flags-answered.definition-dropped: character | in a cod: §2002:4 splits 'character' into four senses (4.26 a code value of a coded character set, 4.27 a graphic character in a screen item, 4.28 a COBOL character, 4.29 a single code value in storage); 2023 drops those entries but keeps each sense under its own term (§2023:3.7 alphanumeric character, national character, §2023:3.93 graphic character, §2023:3.37 COBOL character repertoire), so the drop is of a heading, not of a meaning. GR2 binds inline and out-of-line PERFORM to function identically 'according to the following rules', and in 2002 those include GR10, whose range excludes statements reached by EXIT FUNCTION and EXIT METHOD. 2023 removed both statements (Annex E.2 item 1), its range rule (now GR1, placed BEFORE GR4 so no longer among 'the following rules') names only EXIT PROGRAM and GOBACK. So the 2002 rule covers inline and out-of-line PERFORM ranges left by EXIT FUNCTION/EXIT METHOD, a case the 2023 verdict says nothing about (the 2023 compiler rejects the program). Probe: function FX leaves an inline PERFORM and an out-of-line PERFORM by EXIT FUNCTION, called twice each: --std 2002 prints I1=002 I2=002 O1=020 O2=020 (correct: range ended, no stale return mechanism); --std 2023 refuses with COBOL0902 'the EXIT FUNCTION statement was removed in COBOL-2023'. needs: a 2002 witness for PERFORM ranges left by EXIT FUNCTION and EXIT METHOD (inline and out-of-line). compiler-at-2002: correct for EXIT FUNCTION (probe); EXIT METHOD not probed.
